# Bump stop selection and suspension clearance

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Inspect gap space for droop, consider low-profile stops for tall setups, and ensure upper control arm clearance on IFS. [t1774]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Consider using a low-profile bump stop if standard OEM stops are too tall for an aftermarket setup. [t1774]
- Ensure upper control arm has sufficient bump clearance; hitting limits can affect ride feel and cause bump steer due to extreme angles on the Independent Front Suspension (IFS). [t1774]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Using a low-profile bump stop without verifying if it creates too much gap space compared to an OEM unit. [t1774]
